public_payload.normalized_proposition: The claims that inference is profitable and that most compute goes to training have been disproven, as shown by Anthropic's compute purchases.

statement.excerpt: It’s now very clear that the whole “inference is profitable” and “most compute is being used for training” myths are dead, because if they weren’t, Anthropic would either need way more compute or way higher-quality compute.
statement.document_title: Where Are All The Data Centers?

from_speaker: “most compute is being used for training”
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading rejects two propositions: inference earns more than it costs to serve, and training consumes more than half of compute.
The immediate example is Anthropic, while the wording generalizes to AI labs. Anthropic is therefore the minimum relevant company scope; industry-wide conclusions require broader evidence.
For this ongoing observation without a named reporting period, use January through March 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter before publication.
Profitability requires matched inference receipts and serving costs. Company-wide net losses do not establish inference losses.
Compute means computational resources used, not automatically expenditure. Research expense also need not consist entirely of training.
criteria.support_condition: Matched evidence establishes that inference was not profitable and that training used no more than half of compute in the relevant company scope and target quarter.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Matched evidence establishes positive inference profit or a training share above half. A mixed result requires direct evidence settling the two components in opposite directions.

Anthropic-specific records are required; broader conclusions require equivalent records for a defined set of labs.
